entries.value: "Read-only SQLite, in pure Rust, with a dependency closure of exactly `std` — shared by `graph-materialize` (a build-dependency of 75 crates held to \"serde_json and nothing else\") and `bsc-util` (\"std only, no dependencies\"), both of which must read the record store and neither of which may link rusqlite."

lead: # NO build script and REAL source files, which is deliberate and structural rather than an oversight.
# `graph-materialize/build.rs` `include!`s `src/pages.rs` textually to BOOTSTRAP: it is the script that
# materializes every graph-hosted crate, so it cannot read the store through a crate that has not been
# built yet — and it cannot read the store at all without this reader. A record has no file to include.
# EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. `bsc-util` takes this crate and must still be able to say its
# consumers pay for no third-party compilation; that claim survives only while this line stays empty.
sections.name: [dependencies]

lead: # TESTS ONLY — a dev-dependency is not propagated to anything that links this crate.
# `serde_json` is here to PROVE `json_string_field` against the real library rather than against its
# own output. `rusqlite` is deliberately NOT here even as a dev-dependency: a dev edge still lands in
# the Cargo.lock closure of every dependent, and the sensor binaries' `the_sensor_binary_pulls_in_
# nothing_heavy` guard reads it as a real one. The differential property comes from `testdata/`
# instead — fixtures WRITTEN by the real SQLite engine and committed as bytes.
sections.name: [dev-dependencies]
